### A Prayer to Stack Stones
Author: Jessica Van Roekel
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-prayer/a-prayer-to-stack-stones.html
Passage: Psalm 77:11
Points:
- Present troubles and anxiety can easily cloud our vision and cause us to doubt God's presence.
- Psalm 77 provides a model of vulnerable lament when grief leaves us with only groans.
- The psalmist found peace by intentionally searching his memory for God's past favor.
- Creating tangible reminders of God's deeds helps restore hope when facing new mountains.

### Known Unto God
Author: David C. McCasland
Site: Our Daily Bread
URL: https://military.odb.org/known-unto-god/
Passage: Psalm 77:9
Points:
- Grief and deep suffering can make believers feel isolated and forgotten.
- Like Asaph, we may struggle with painful fears that God has withheld His mercy.
- The remedy for feelings of abandonment is meditating on what God has done in the past.
- God never forgets His people and provides an oasis of comfort in every trial.

### ‘My Soul Refuses to Be Comforted’: A Song for Long Nights in Darkness
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/my-soul-refuses-to-be-comforted
Passage: Psalm 77:1-20
Points:
- Crises of faith can produce sleepless nights where the soul refuses easy consolation.
- Asaph demonstrates how to bring honest, anguished questions directly to the Lord.
- When present circumstances appear hopeless, the remedy is looking backward to God's historical deeds.
- Remembering Red Sea-level redemptive power anchors our trust in God's future grace.
- Even without immediate resolution to our pain, recounting God's character sustains enduring faith.
